paragraphs.en: {Popularization} has in some cases {changed} the original meaning of emotional intelligence.Many people now {misunderstand} emotional intelligence as almost everything {desirable} in a person's {makeup} that cannot be measured by an {IQ} test, such as character, motivation, confidence, mental {stability} , {optimism} and “people skills.”People tend to interpret, for example, being {shy} as a representation of low EQ.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 大众化 </u> 在某些情况下已经 <u> 改变 </u> 了情商原本的含义。现在，许多人 <u> 误解 </u> 了情商，认为它涵盖了一个人 <u> 性格 </u> 中几乎所有无法通过 <u> 智商 </u> 测试来衡量的 <u> 可取 </u> 之处，如品格、动机、自信、心理 <u> 稳定性 </u> 、 <u> 乐观 </u> 和”人际交往能力”。例如，人们往往把 <u> 害羞 </u> 解读为情商低的一种表现。

paragraphs.en: In fact, EQ is about recognizing, understanding, and managing emotions—both one's own and those of others.When an employee is preparing for an important presentation, he might feel {embarrassed} to admit his anxiety, so he {dresses} in his best suit, complete with a sharp {jacket} .But he {sweats} a lot and constantly adjusts his {belt} .A manager with high emotional intelligence would notice these cues and offer support for the public presentation.
paragraphs.cn: 事实上，情商就是认识、理解和管理情绪，包括自己和他人的情绪。当一名员工在准备一个重要的演讲时，他可能 <u> 不好意思 </u> 承认自己的焦虑，于是他 <u> 穿上 </u> 自己最好的西装，配上利落的 <u> 夹克 </u> 。但他却 <u> 汗流 </u> 浃背，不停地调整他的 <u> 腰带 </u> 。高情商的管理者会注意到这些线索，并为这次公开演讲提供帮助。

paragraphs.en: Emotional intelligence is a specific set of skills that can be used for either good or bad purposes.The ability to {accurately} understand how others are feeling may be used by a {doctor} to find out how best to help her patients, while a {cheater} might use it to control potential {victims} .Being {emotionally} intelligent does not necessarily make one a moral person.
paragraphs.cn: 情商是一组特定的技能，可以用于好的或坏的目的。 <u> 医生 </u> 可能利用 <u> 准确 </u> 理解他人感受的能力，找到帮助病人的最佳方法，而 <u> 骗子 </u> 则可能利用这种能力操控潜在的 <u> 受害者 </u> 。 <u> 情 </u> 商高并不一定意味着一个人是有道德的人。

paragraphs.en: Popular beliefs {regarding} emotional intelligence run far {ahead} of what research can {reasonably} support, and even serve as a modern {justice} for human development.Some might {protest} its widespread adoption, but despite some {mostly} understood aspects and {prejudices} surrounding the concept, the {overall} effects of the {publicity} have been more {beneficial} than harmful.The most positive aspect of this popularization is a new and much needed emphasis on {mercy} and empathy by {employers} , {educators} and others interested in {promoting} social {well-being} .For example, instead of focusing solely on academic achievements, schools now {restore} balance by prioritizing emotional learning.The popularization has helped both the {public} and researchers re-evaluate the {functionality} of emotions and how they serve people {adaptively} in {everyday} life.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 关于 </u> 情商的流行观念远远 <u> 超出 </u> 了研究所能 <u> 合理 </u> 支持的范畴，它甚至成为人类发展的现代 <u> 公理 </u> 。有些人可能会 <u> 反对 </u> 情商概念的广泛使用，然而，围绕这一概念，且不论那些 <u> 通常 </u> 人们了解的方面和 <u> 偏见 </u> ，其 <u> 宣传 </u> 推广所带来的 <u> 总体 </u> 影响却是 <u> 利 </u> 大于弊的。普及”情商”概念最积极的一面在于， <u> 雇主 </u> 、 <u> 教育工作者 </u> 和其他有志于 <u> 推动 </u> 社会 <u> 福祉 </u> 的人开始重视 <u> 仁慈 </u> 和同理心，而这种重视是极为必要的。例如，学校现在不再只关注学业成绩，而是优先考虑情绪学习，以此来 <u> 恢复 </u> 平衡的状态。这种普及有助于 <u> 公众 </u> 和研究人员重新评估情绪的 <u> 功能 </u> ，以及情绪在 <u> 日常 </u> 生活中如何 <u> 适应性地 </u> 服务大众。

paragraphs.en: Although the continuing popular appeal of emotional intelligence is desirable, we hope that such attention will {excite} a {reform} in the scientific and {scholarly} study of emotion.It is our hope that in the coming {decades} , {advances} in science will provide a {worthy} framework for understanding and managing emotions.Emotional intelligence, with its focus on both head and heart, may serve to {point} us in the right direction.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管情商持续受到大众欢迎是一件好事，但我们希望，这种关注能 <u> 激发 </u> 情绪的科学和 <u> 学术 </u> 研究方面的 <u> 改革 </u> 。我们希望，在未来的几 <u> 十年 </u> 里，科学的各种 <u> 进步 </u> 将为理解和管理情绪提供 <u> 值得 </u> （借鉴）的框架。情商概念同时关注了头脑与心灵，它可能会为我们 <u> 指明 </u> 正确的方向。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
